decisions.quote:
In order to further investigate the relationship between psychopathy, aggression, narcissism, and selfesteem, Falkenbach, Howe, and Falki (2013) recruited 118
undergraduates for the purpose of assessing how selfesteem relates to psychopathy and narcissism, and to determine the predictive value of the two latter constructs
on aggression. Their results suggested a positive correlation between high levels of PPI-I and healthy narcissism,
alongside high self-esteem and low aggression. At the
opposite end, individuals with high levels of PPI-II and
pathological narcissism displayed lower self-esteem and
higher aggression. The purpose of the present study is to
replicate the previous ﬁndings to further conﬁrm the relationship between psychopathy, narcissism, aggression, and
self-esteem in a community sample.
decisions.reason: The dependent original study identity is unambiguously resolved to Falkenbach, Howe, and Falki (2013), 'Using self-esteem to disaggregate psychopathy, narcissism, and aggression' (DOI: 10.1016/j.paid.2012.12.017). The present study recruits a new sample of 127 community participants (Method, lines 131-139) to re-test the published findings that Falkenbach et al. (2013) originally obtained in 118 undergraduates. Because new data were collected in an independent sample to re-test a specific published finding, both the shipped record and blind coding correctly classify the type as 'replication'.
